channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: "Israel and Hezbollah agree to a ceasefire," senior US official tells Reuters
item.description: Citing a senior US official on Friday, Reuters reported that Israel and Hezbollah have agreed to a ceasefire at 4 p.m. local time on Friday.

item.title: Oil: Strait of Hormuz reopening steadies crude prices– UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research reports that Oil prices stabilized after comments from US Vice President JD Vance confirmed tankers carrying over 12 million barrels had crossed the Strait of Hormuz. Brent closed at $79.85 and WTI at $76.60.

item.title: Gold heads for third weekly loss as hawkish Fed overshadows US-Iran initial peace deal
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains under pressure on Friday as traders assess the latest news about the US-Iran peace deal and the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,157 after hitting a one-week low of $4,121 earlier in the day.

item.title: British Pound: Pound hit by BoE hold and cautious outlook – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research reports that GBP/USD fell sharply after the Bank of England left rates unchanged at 3.75%, before trimming losses to trade near 1.3236. The BOE decision saw a 7–2 vote, with two members preferring a hike to 4.00%.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise on fresh highs – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research strategist Chang Wei Liang notes that USD/JPY has broken above 161, returning to levels that previously triggered official action.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise on Fed stance – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research notes that the US Dollar extended gains after the Fed’s hawkish hold, pushing USD/JPY sharply higher to 161.37. The pair is now trading near levels that previously triggered Japanese authorities’ intervention.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Upside case from flows and yields – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that foreign investors sharply increased purchases of long-term US securities in April, with inflows over the past year more than offsetting the US trade deficit.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: NEER strength caps upside for USD/SGD – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research notes that USD/SGD closed at 1.2900, with the Singapore Dollar Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (S$NEER) estimated at 1.75% above its mid-point.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD nears $4,100 as Fed tightening bets rise
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends losses for the third consecutive day on Friday, hitting one-week lows at $4,121, on track to close a three-week losing streak.

item.title: Euro: Dollar strength keeps pair under pressure – UOB
item.description: According to UOB Global Economics & Markets Research, EUR/USD extended its recent decline as the US Dollar index hit a one-year high following the Fed’s hawkish hold.

item.title: Brent Oil: Lower prices ease Asia FX pressures – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Chang Wei Liang points out that an interim US–Iran agreement has reopened the Strait of Hormuz, allowing traffic to resume while talks continue.

item.title: United States Dollar: Upside scope seen but limits in view – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes the US Dollar has extended gains after a record hawkish shift in the Fed’s dot plot, even as Oil remains sharply lower over the past month.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise on US holiday – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note that the Dollar has held post-Fed gains, keeping USD/JPY elevated in intervention territory.

item.title: Gold: Fed hawkishness and Dollar strength weigh on prices – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research highlights that Gold eased as hawkish Fed signals and a stronger US Dollar pressured the metal. An interim US–Iran ceasefire reduced inflation fears and contributed to softer Oil, further dampening Gold’s appeal as an inflation hedge.

item.title: British Pound: By-election uncertainty weighs on Pound – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research strategist Chang Wei Liang warns that GBP/USD could stay volatile after easing towards 1.32, as Labour’s Burnham leads the Makerfield by‑election.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Limited downside as SNB stays cautious – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny says the Swiss Franc underperformed after the SNB left rates at zero, but only minor inflation forecast revisions underline expectations of persistently low Swiss inflation.

item.title: Euro: Higher year-end target on softer Dollar view – ING
item.description: ING’s FX team, led by Francesco Pesole, has updated its EUR/USD projections, now targeting 1.18 by year-end. They expect moderate Dollar depreciation in the third and fourth quarters, helped by a dovish Fed relative to market pricing and fading energy sensitivity.

item.title: Euro edges up from three-month lows as US Dollar buyers take a breather
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades practically flat against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, changing hands at 1.1460 after bouncing up from three-month lows at 1.1420.

item.title: Japanese Yen within touch of forty-year lows as intervention talk heats up
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) remains under pressure against the US Dollar (USD), with the USD/JPY pair trading near multi-decade highs and closing in on the 2024 peak around 162.00.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Lower Oil eases pressure on Yen – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that USD/JPY is trading just below its multi-decade high but argues that the recent slump in Oil prices should relieve some pressure on the Japanese Yen.

item.title: Bank of England: Active hold stance supports restrictive convergence – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Daily notes that the Bank of England kept rates unchanged in what policymakers call an “active hold,” effectively tightening policy versus pre‑war expectations for cuts.

item.title: British Pound: Political risks cap recovery – BBH
item.description: Elias Haddad at Brown Brothers Harriman writes that GBP/USD has bounced after holding above its late-March low, but he sees risks still tilted lower.

item.title: WTI pauses its decline as Crude shipments resume through the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $75.60 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.21% on the day, but remains under pressure after the sharp decline seen this week.

item.title: United States Dollar Index (DXY) eases from 101.13 highs but remains near yearly highs
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the Greenback against a basket of peers, has lost steam during Friday’s European session, with markets at half throttle amid the Juneteenth bank holiday in the US and investors pondering the soundness of the US-Iran peace deal.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.06 per troy ounce, down 0.99% from the $65.71 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Fails ahead of 0.8100/YTD peak; bullish potential intact
item.description: The USD/CHF pair builds on this week's solid rebound from the 0.7900 mark and gains strong follow-through positive traction for the third consecutive day on Friday.

item.title: British Pound: Trendline break points to deeper losses – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts, led by Kenneth Broux, report that GBP/USD has broken below its ascending trendline from April 2025 and is extending declines toward the March low.

item.title: Global rates: Converging at slightly restrictive levels – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Daily stresses that unchanged rates in the UK and US contrast with recent hikes by the ECB and Bank of Japan, but argues this is less divergence than it appears.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Breakout fuelled by hawkish Fed repricing – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that the Dollar is in breakout territory after DXY moved above 101.00, supported by a hawkish shift in Fed expectations.

item.title: Oil: Strait of Hormuz risks ease but fees loom – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank highlights that a 60‑day US–Iran memorandum of understanding has reduced immediate risks to the global economy by keeping the Strait of Hormuz open, though ship crossings remain limited.
